av_event.line_text: Yeah. No, that's fair, that. That's a better way of doing it than mine, to be honest. My sister says I've got no tact.
av_event.what: Behind Ryan, one of the unframed gig posters above the single bed comes loose from its Blu Tack at a top corner and flops down, so it hangs diagonally against the pale grey wall for the rest of the call. Ryan doesn't turn round.

text:
A: Alright! Gemma, is it? Can you hear me?
B: Hiya. Yeah. Yeah, I can hear you.
A: Sound. Ryan, Stockport. You're my last one, so no pressure, you've got to be the best.
B: *(laughs)* Oh no.
A: I'm joking. Everyone's been sound. Where are you, then?
B: Walsall. Bloxwich.
A: Black Country! Is it true you lot say "yam yam"?
B: Erm, some people say it. My granddad did. I don't really.
A: Fair enough. What do you do?
B: I run a shift. Parcel depot, off the M6. Late shift.
A: Late shift, so you know the knackered feeling. I do lock-up at two some nights and I'm getting a cab home, costs me a fortune. How many people have you got?
B: About forty.
A: Forty, that's more than me. I've got eighteen and they're a nightmare. Do you get people not turning up? That's my whole life. Lads ringing in at four o'clock, "I've got a migraine." You haven't got a migraine, mate, you've got Leeds Fest tickets.
B: *(laughs)* Yeah. Every Monday. Somebody's nan's always poorly.
A: The nan! Classic. How do you deal with it? Do you go in hard? 'Cause I go in hard, I'm blunt, me.
B: Erm, not really. I sort of try and talk to them first. Sometimes there's something going on, do you know what I mean. Had a lad last year, kept being late, and it turned out his mum was ill and he was doing everything at home. So you can't just go in hard on that.
A: Yeah. No, that's fair, that. That's a better way of doing it than mine, to be honest. My sister says I've got no tact.
B: Sorry, I didn't mean you were doing it wrong.
A: No, you're right, though! I'll nick that. Here, are you a music person? I ask everyone.
B: Erm, nineties and two-thousands stuff. Indie, R&B. I have the same playlist on for months. I don't really go to gigs any more, the crowds wear me out.
A: See, you'd be alright at mine, it's small, nobody's elbowing you. What's on the playlist, go on?
B: Erm, Arctic Monkeys. Destiny's Child. Bit of Craig David.
A: Craig David! Proper. I've got Born to Do It on vinyl on that shelf somewhere.
B: *(laughs)* Have you? My husband's called Craig, he hates it when I put that on.
A: Everyone's called Craig today. I had a Craig earlier, Pools fan, sound lad.
B: Yeah, I had him first. He was nice.
A: What else do you do, when you're not on a late?
B: Walk the dog. That's her, Dolly. Jigsaws. And a pub quiz with my sister once a month.
A: Jigsaws. I couldn't. I'd lose a piece in five minutes and launch it out the window.
B: I've had one on the go three weeks. It's all sky. *(laughs)*
A: All sky! Why would you do that to yourself?
B: I don't know, to be fair. It's sort of calming. You just sit there, and nobody's asking you for anything.
A: Yeah, that I get, actually. That's me with the records. I put one on and—
